extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers, journals, editors, reviewers, authors, and platform developers
extracted.subtask_description: High-level principles and functional requirements for an open peer-review and publishing platform intended for conferences, journals, and other reviewing entities. Covers openness dimensions (reviewing, access, discussion), technical features (API, distributed hosting), community metadata (directory, COI), and licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide a configurable platform for peer review that generalizes over many subtle gradations of openness, allowing conference organizers, journals, and other "reviewing entities" to configure the specific policy of their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as a testbed for different policies to help scientific communities experiment with open scholarship while addressing legitimate concerns regarding confidentiality, attribution, and bias. Emphasizes configurability so venues can choose degree of openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Track submissions, coordinate the efforts of editors, reviewers and authors, and host… Sharded and distributed for speed and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide submission tracking, editorial/reviewer/author coordination, and reliable hosting infrastructure (sharded/distributed) to support publication workflows at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Free access to papers for all, free paper submissions. No fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no paywalls and no submission fees so papers are freely accessible and contribution is not gated by cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting of accepted papers, with their reviews, comments. Continued discussion forum associated with the paper post acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support ongoing post-acceptance discussion; allow publication venue chairs/editors to control the structure of review/comment forms, read/write access, and timing of discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Directory
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of people, with conflict-of-interest information, including institutions and relations, such as co-authors, co-PIs, co-workers, advisors/advisees, and family connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain structured directory metadata to record COI-relevant relations and institutional affiliations to assist in conflict management and reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Models of scientific topics and expertise. Directory of people includes scientific expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reviewer-paper matching and recommendation functionality for large-scale conferences: incorporate expertise models, bidding, constraints, and various reviewer-balancing strategies; offer paper recommendations to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open API
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide a simple REST API for accessing and uploading records of people, their groupings, document content, invitations and reviewing assignments, conflict-of-interest designations, and reviewing workflow patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose automation capabilities (track submissions, monitor review process, send customized bulk email, automate workflow actions) with a clear, robust model of read/write permissions so scripts and integrations can be built safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Source
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenReview web interface is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms under the terms of the GNU Affero General Public License v3. The source code is available on GitHub. Many other parts of the OpenReview platform are also open source...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AGPLv3 licensing, public GitHub repositories, and transparent code release practices; note that some further releases are pending a professional security review of the codebase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission, Governance, and Sponsorship Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview is a long-term project to advance science through improved peer review with legal nonprofit status. We gratefully acknowledge the support of the great diversity of OpenReview Sponsors ––scientific peer review is sacrosanct, and should not be owned by any one sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the platform as a nonprofit, community-oriented initiative; emphasize independence from single-sponsor control and acknowledgement of diverse support.
